reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses toughening mechanisms in Cantor alloy and precipitate formation in CoCrFeMnNi-based HEAs, but neither addresses MnNiSi-based alloys, V additions, or magnetocaloric properties. The key premises about V-rich precipitate formation, their effect on toughness, and preservation of magnetocaloric effect are entirely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: V addition forms fine, well-dispersed V-rich intermetallic precipitates in MnNiSi
These precipitates act as barriers to crack propagation, enhancing toughness
The precipitates form without significantly modifying the magnetocaloric matrix composition or ordering
The magnetocaloric effect is preserved in the presence of these precipitates
Annealing at ~550°C is sufficient to nucleate these precipitates
